activity.notes: Batista seized power in the 10 March 1952 coup before formally assuming the presidency on 4 April. ATLAS therefore models the whole second regime as de facto military rule from the coup through his flight from Cuba on 1 January 1959, rather than presenting the coup phase as an ordinary constitutional presidential term.

sources.title: Historical Documents - Cuba
sources.citation_text: The U.S. State Department records Batista's 1940 presidency, retirement at the end of his term in 1944, and seizure of power by army coup in 1952.

sources.title: Editorial Note on the 1952 Cuban coup
sources.citation_text: The U.S. State Department records Batista's coup on 10 March 1952 and notes that he became President on 4 April 1952.

sources.title: Fulgencio Batista
sources.citation_text: The standard office chronology records the elected presidency from 10 October 1940 to 10 October 1944 and his second period of rule ending 1 January 1959.
